questions.question: Which two countries led the main rival blocs during the Cold War?
choices: Britain and France
United States and Soviet Union
China and Japan
Germany and Italy

questions.question: What did the term Iron Curtain describe?
choices: The division between Soviet-dominated eastern Europe and the West
A trade barrier around the entire Pacific Ocean
A defensive wall between Canada and the United States
The border separating India from Pakistan

questions.question: Which alliance was established in 1949 for collective defense among the United States, Canada, and several European countries?
choices: Warsaw Pact
League of Nations
European Union
NATO

questions.question: Which alliance linked the Soviet Union with several eastern European states beginning in 1955?
choices: NATO
SEATO
Warsaw Pact
OPEC

questions.question: What was the Berlin Airlift of 1948–1949?
choices: An effort to supply West Berlin by air during a blockade
A campaign to bomb East Berlin after reunification
An evacuation of every German city
An invasion of Germany by neutral states

questions.question: Which event brought the United States and Soviet Union close to nuclear conflict in 1962?
choices: Suez Crisis
Cuban Missile Crisis
Hungarian uprising
Berlin Wall's fall

questions.question: What did détente mean in Cold War diplomacy?
choices: The merger of rival military alliances
The surrender of all nuclear weapons
An easing of tensions between rival powers
The end of diplomatic negotiations

questions.question: Why is the conflict called a cold war despite wars in Korea and Vietnam?
choices: All conflicts occurred in cold climates
There were no combat deaths during the period
Every dispute was resolved by trade agreements
The superpowers avoided direct full-scale war against each other

questions.question: What was the central purpose of the U.S. policy of containment?
choices: To limit the spread of Soviet influence and communism
To prohibit all contact with European governments
To place every country under direct American rule
To restore European colonies after independence

questions.question: How did the Marshall Plan relate to Cold War competition?
choices: It required western Europe to join the Warsaw Pact
It supported European recovery and strengthened ties with the United States
It financed the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan
It replaced every European national government

questions.question: Why did East German authorities build the Berlin Wall in 1961?
choices: To mark Germany's peaceful reunification
To stop western tourists from entering all of Europe
To defend Berlin from an ongoing French invasion
To prevent large-scale departures to the West

questions.question: How did nuclear deterrence affect superpower behavior?
choices: It guaranteed that neither side would develop weapons
It made conventional conflicts impossible
The prospect of devastating retaliation discouraged direct attack
It transferred military decisions to the United Nations alone

questions.question: What did nonaligned governments generally seek during the Cold War?
choices: Independence from formal alignment with either major bloc
Membership in both NATO and the Warsaw Pact
A return to colonial rule by European powers
The abolition of their own national governments

questions.question: Why are some Cold War conflicts described as proxy wars?
choices: Only unmanned machines participated in them
Rival powers supported local sides without directly fighting each other at full scale
They involved no local political goals
They were fought solely through economic statistics

questions.question: What was a global effect of Cold War competition in science and technology?
choices: An agreement to stop satellite development
The elimination of military research spending
The abandonment of space exploration by both sides
An intensified space race and investment in research

questions.question: Which Cold War sequence is correctly ordered?
choices: Cuban Missile Crisis → Berlin Airlift → Berlin Wall falls
Berlin Wall falls → Berlin Airlift → Cuban Missile Crisis
Berlin Airlift → Cuban Missile Crisis → Berlin Wall falls
Berlin Airlift → Berlin Wall falls → Cuban Missile Crisis

questions.question: Why is it incomplete to explain a Cold War-era civil war only as a superpower contest?
choices: Local histories and political goals also shaped the conflict
Local groups had no influence on the fighting
All governments followed the same economic system
The superpowers never provided assistance abroad

questions.question: Two rival powers negotiate limits on nuclear weapons while remaining political opponents. Which concept best fits?
choices: Decolonization
Détente
Annexation
Autarky

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes the fall of the Berlin Wall from the dissolution of the Soviet Union?
choices: Both occurred before NATO was founded
The Soviet Union dissolved decades before the wall was built
The wall opened in 1989; the Soviet Union dissolved in 1991
The wall opened after the Soviet Union joined NATO

questions.question: Which source pairing would best help compare how the rival blocs presented the same Cold War event?
choices: Trade statistics from countries not involved in the event
A later summary based only on one government's archives
Military equipment lists without discussion of the event
Contemporary American and Soviet newspaper reports
